items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Bobby Trumpet asked me to play with him... I went to work with him right away. And I stayed with him five years.

ctx.x: Tajoe was Taje, the next job was Reno, and I had just left these towns with Nat, and I just -- it was so vivid on my mind of being with Nat, I would sign his name sometimes because you know when you work these clubs when you're with a certain act you get a discount, you know. I signed John Collins, Nat Cole, or John Collins, Patti Page. And I found myself signing Nat's name.

And I quit. I put my notice in I just couldn't go through that. You know, it was just kind of anticlimatic, you know. Yeah. So I loved her but no. So I -- while I was rehearsing with her Bobby Trumpet asked me to play with him, as a matter of fact I went out to see him at Whitting Hills, and I told him that I would like to play with him but I was committed to Patti. I would prefer playing with him but I had been rehearsing with her and I couldn't. He said, you know, I admire you for being loyal to Patti, he said,…

So when I left Patti I let him know that I was free and I went to work with him right away. And I stayed with him five years. Very -- five years, and it was a very pleasant association. But -- and he was admired as I said by all musicians, black, white, they all loved Bobby, so consequently they would all come in to see Bobby, and to hear me. And I got quite -- it was kind of gratifying and reward-

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: being with Bobby, and getting a chance to play... I did the Lucy Show... I agreed to do the Today Show with us

ctx.x: That was '65 and '70. Well, what happened, I'll tell you how I went with Bobby.
It was after 1970 when I saw you with him at China Trader.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Bobby Trump Troop. Boy, I tell you, that is very good, isn't it? I never saw this.

ctx.x: Yeah, well I -- let's see. I didn't know this, I'd never heard of this. Booker Collins, Coleman, Williams, Lee Collins. I knew Lee Collins, I used to work with Lee Collins. I was in New Orleans Lee Collins. He was a very good trumpet player. I worked with him around Chicago. I think all of the New York -- I don't mean New York, the New Orleans trumpet players eventually wound up in Chicago. There was another one -- They went up the river? MS. WILLARD: (Inaudible).

That's right. There was another one by Guy Kelly, a very good trumpet player. Punch Miller, who played with Francois' band there. And of course Lee Collins. I played quite a bit with him. I don't see my name here. Yeah, I see Booker Collins and -- oh, John -- oh, Albert, I see. That's why. You know John Albert Collins? MS. WILLARD: (Inaudible).
